D016_m001.question:
"I'm really struggling, doctor. It's been going on for… well, forever, it feels like, but it’s gotten so much worse in the last year or so. At work, I'm a sales manager, and everything has to be just *so*. If a display isn't perfectly symmetrical or if the mannequins aren't facing exactly the right way, I can't focus on anything else. I'll spend ages adjusting them, even if it means staying late. 

At home, it's the same thing. My spices, my books… they all have to be lined up perfectly, or I get this intense feeling of unease, like something bad will happen if they're not. It's not just a preference; it's a *need*. I know it sounds silly, and I try to stop, but the anxiety just builds until I fix it. It’s exhausting, and it’s really starting to affect my life outside of work. I've missed dinners with friends because I was still arranging things. I just want it to stop."
D016_m001.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Specific Phobia

D016_m002.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a persistent thing, honestly, for as long as I can rightly remember, but it seems to have gotten a fair bit worse since Martha passed a couple of years back. I find myself spending hours just… arranging things. The books on the shelf, the ornaments on the mantelpiece, even the cans in the pantry – they all have to be perfectly spaced, perfectly aligned. If they’re off by even a millimeter, I get this awful feeling, like a knot in my stomach, and I just can’t seem to rest until it's 'just right.'

And leaving the house, or even just going from one room to another, has become a real ordeal. I have to go through doorways a certain number of times, usually three, before I feel like it's "safe" to continue. It sounds daft, I know, but if I don't, I get this relentless worry that something terrible will happen. It’s gotten to the point where even simple errands take me ages, and frankly, I’m exhausted by it all. It’s hard to enjoy my retirement when I'm constantly battling these urges."
D016_m002.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Specific Phobia

D016_m005.question:

D016_m006.question:

And the cleaning… it’s become an obsession. Every time I touch something, I feel dirty. I wash my hands until they’re raw, multiple times an hour, even when I know there’s no real reason to. My bathroom has practically become a shrine to antibacterial wipes. I used to love gardening, but now I spend more time washing up than I do tending to the roses. It’s exhausting, and it keeps me from doing the things I actually want to do."
D016_m006.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
